newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Moslem refugees return to Bosnia from Serbia.
newsitem.headline: Moslem refugees return to Bosnia from Serbia.

text.p: A group of 27 Moslem refugees who sheltered in Serbia during the Bosnian war returned to Sarajevo by bus on Thursday, the first such group to be repatriated, government officials said.
One man, 51-year-old Omer Borcak, explained why he had gone to Belgrade after being driven from his home in Rudo, eastern Bosnia, by separatist Serbs in 1992.

"I was expelled. In that period the road to Belgrade was the only one open. In Belgrade we lived with our cousins. Now I will live in Sarajevo with my sister, brothers and my mother," he told Reuters.
Separatist Serb forces drove hundreds of thousands of Moslems from their homes in towns like Rudo when war erupted in the spring of 1992.
By the time the war had run its course in December 1995 Moslems, Serbs and Croats comprising at least half the country's population had been uprooted. Some remained in Bosnia but many fled abroad.
Only a few Moslems like Borcak ended up in Serbia, whose political leadership actively fomented and supported the Bosnian war on behalf of separatist Bosnian Serbs.
A young Moslem from Jajce who was attending school in Belgrade when the war started and stayed there said his experience as a refugee had been mixed.
"I had no problems with legal authorities there, but I suffered from quite a lot of provocations from civilians," Ragib Mestrovac, 23, said.

"We are expecting more refugees within the next months. Some 800 to 900 refugees want to return to Bosnia from Serbia," said Nedzib Lipljankic, an official from Bosnia's Moslem-Croat federation ministry for refugees.
